properties.description:

continues.

properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

unstable and unsafe.

Report flooding to the National Weather Service by calling toll free,
800 401 9535, when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
FFWILN

The National Weather Service in Wilmington has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Fayette County in central Ohio...
Greene County in west central Ohio...

* Until 1130 PM EDT.

* At 906 PM EDT, radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy rain
across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 2.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Beavercreek, Xenia, Bellbrook, Cedarville, Jamestown, Wilberforce,
New Jasper, Spring Valley, Bowersville, Paintersville, Oldtown,
Trebein, Greene County Airport, Bell Center and Rosemoor.

This includes I-71 in Ohio between mile markers 60 and 63.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

To report flash flooding, go to our website at weather.gov/iln and
submit your report via social media, when you can do so safely.
